author: sunfishcode
body:
Generalize get_nullable_type to accept types that have an all-ones bit
pattern as their sentry "null" value.

This will allow [`OwnedFd`], [`BorrowedFd`], [`OwnedSocket`], and
[`BorrowedSocket`] to be marked with
`#[rustc_nonnull_optimization_guaranteed]`, which will allow
`Option<OwnedFd>`, `Option<BorrowedFd>`, `Option<OwnedSocket>`, and
`Option<BorrowedSocket>` to be used in FFI declarations, as described
in the [I/O safety RFC].

For example, it will allow a function like `open` on Unix and `WSASocketW`
on Windows to be declared using `Option<OwnedFd>` and `Option<OwnedSocket>`
return types, respectively.

The actual change to add `#[rustc_nonnull_optimization_guaranteed]`
to the abovementioned types will be a separate PR, as it'll depend on
having this patch in the stage0 compiler.

Also, update the diagnostics to mention that "niche optimizations" are
used in libstd as well as libcore, as `rustc_layout_scalar_valid_range_start`
and `rustc_layout_scalar_valid_range_end` are already in use in libstd.

[`OwnedFd`]: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/c9dc44be24c58ff13ce46416c4b97ab5c1bd8429/library/std/src/os/fd/owned.rs#L49
[`BorrowedFd`]: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/c9dc44be24c58ff13ce46416c4b97ab5c1bd8429/library/std/src/os/fd/owned.rs#L29
[`OwnedSocket`]: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/c9dc44be24c58ff13ce46416c4b97ab5c1bd8429/library/std/src/os/windows/io/socket.rs#L51
[`BorrowedSocket`]: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/c9dc44be24c58ff13ce46416c4b97ab5c1bd8429/library/std/src/os/windows/io/socket.rs#L29
[I/O safety RFC]: https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/3128-io-safety.md#ownedfd-and-borrowedfdfd-1

author: vmoroz
body:
## The issue
Currently `Reference` finalizers are run inside of `SetImmediate`.
In case if user code creates a lot of native objects in the main script, it could cause a significant memory pressure, even if the objects are properly released. This is because they are "collected" only inside of `SetImmediate` that follows the script run. 
See issue: https://github.com/nodejs/node-addon-api/issues/1140

In the https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/[REDACTED:gitleaks] commit the processing of finalizers was moved from the GC second pass to the `SetImmediate` because finalizers may throw JavaScript exceptions which can affect behavior of other functions.
If the JavaScript exception is thrown inside of `SetImmediate`, then it causes an unhandled exception which can be handled process-wide with help of `process.on('uncaughtException', ...)` event handler.

## The solution
In this PR we are switching back to processing finalizers in the GC second pass which may happen any time after GC calls.
To address the issue of handling JS exceptions from finalizers we do the following in this PR:
- By default, all JS exceptions from finalizers cause the Node.js unhandled exceptions. We apply the same error handling mechanism as used by immediate tasks created by `SetImmediate`. Thus, we address the previous issue with the finalizer JS errors interrupting other functions, and align the error handling behavior with `SetImmediate`.
- In addition to it, we are adding new `node_api_set_finalizer_error_handler` public API to setup an error handler per `napi_env` instance which is created per each native module. Each native module can handle its finalizer JS errors on its own.

## Tests
New test_finalizer_exception test is added to js-native-api to verify the new behavior.
All other js-native-api, node-api, and cctests are passing.

## Documentation
The n-api.md documentation is updated with the new `node_api_set_finalizer_error_handler` public API.
See the n-api.md for the details about the `node_api_set_finalizer_error_handler` function.

author: periodic
body:
# Overview

Loops in symlinks could cause the discovery to loop forever.  This change uses the file/device ID instead of the path when determining when to recurse.

## Acceptance criteria

Cyclic directory tree (via symbolic links) can be analyzed by FOSSA CLI successfully.

## Testing plan

Tests were added for an example case provided which triggered this behavior.  That case has been encoded as a unit test.

```
.
└── lib
    ├── pg
    │   └── lib -> ..
    └── sqlite
        ├── example.txt
        └── lib -> ..
```

## Risks

This change relies on the `PosixCompat` library to handle cross-platform execution.  There's a chance that this leads to unexpected behavior.  Our testing suite should catch much of this.  In any case that it may be incorrect we are unlikely to run into issues because the IDs being used are just for checking what was visited and so just have to be unique and stable within a execution.

## References

This structure is typically used by [shards](https://crystal-lang.org/reference/1.3/the_shards_command/index.html#usage) dependency manager. As such, CLI discovery will fail, when CLI encounters projects managed by shards.

Support for Shards is still pending: https://github.com/fossas/fossa-cli/issues/189

author: stuhood
body:
#13112 is porting more operations on `Digest`/`Snapshot` to use of `DigestTrie` in order to reduce IO by allowing them to operate entirely in memory.

When we have a `DigestTrie` in memory, we are able to persist all of its recursive `remexec::Directory` structures in parallel. To that end, this change adds batch persistence to the local LMDB store, which allows us to use a single context switch and write transaction (*per LMDB shard) to persist an entire `DigestTrie`.

author: lukesteensen
body:
Fixes #10412

It turns out that the fix for #9173 in #9536 was based on a misunderstanding of the underlying issue. In that commit, I noted that:

> When replacing the upstream component, the new input for the rebuilt downstream component has not yet been registered and therefore doesn't get readded to the rebuilt `Fanout`.

It's correct that the new input has not yet been registered, but it misses that the previous version of the input is still present and does get readded to the rebuilt `Fanout`. This is because we only remove existing inputs for components that are being removed from the topology entirely.

The actual issue in that case stemmed from the logic we have to reuse buffers for rebuilt sinks where the buffer config itself has not changed. To facilitate that reuse, we removed the existing input of the sink (i.e. the buffer sender) in order to stash it in a collection of buffers to be passed along and reused later in the reload process. This created a special case where the previous input actually would not be present and therefore not readded to a rebuilt `Fanout` that previously contained it.

The fix we implemented for that issue (based on the misunderstood cause) was to send `Add` instead of `Replace` messages to `Fanout`s that had been rebuilt when the downstream component itself was being rebuilt. This worked for sinks that fell into the category described above, but created issues for other types of components whose inputs were not removed. That is the direct cause of #10412, where we're sending an `Add` message for a rebuilt transform when its previous input was already present.

This change undoes the previous fix and makes it so we simply don't remove the input for sinks that are being rebuilt. This eliminates the special case and lets the original logic work fine in both scenarios.

| ------------- | ---
| Bug fix?      | yes
| New feature?  | no
| BC breaks?    | no
| Deprecations? | no

| Fixed tickets | #8980

NetworkPort's prepareInputForUpdate was calling `NetworkPort::splitInputForElements` which was removing all non-fields that didn't start with an underscore. This meant that the `update` input was being removed and later in the update method, it was failing that check which would have cleared the saved input.

This fix I propose sets the `_update` property in `CommonDBTM::update` just before `prepareInputForUpdate` is called while leaving the original `update` property. Then afterwards, the `update` property is removed. This should fix the reported issue without too much risk in causing a break in compatibility.

In addition, AWS SDK can automatically calculate a checksum as it streams data into S3

Adding `--asyncio-mode=auto` to the pytest run.

author: rtrg
body:
Currently on page load, all placeholder cells' widget are being rendered immediately irrespective of whether user is interacting with UI or not.

This is because currently on every cell's widget (numberCellsToRenderDirectly) insert, there is a requestIdleCallback registered to render a placeholder cells' widget (which is enabled when observer is present) and its timeout is specified as 1 second. On page load, initial cells' widget (numberCellsToRenderDirectly) gets rendered and each of them will trigger a renderPlaceholderCells in a short span and given all of them have timeout: 1000 ms, they are going to render almost together and more over it is not using idle time left which means even if 100 cells are queued then irrespective of idle time left (which is generally <50ms during active rendering) it will try to render all the 100 cells which might hinder actual user interaction.
For each scheduled place holder cell's widget rendered it will register more callbacks which is making all the cells to render as soon as page loads making the numberCellsToRenderDirectly setting not so useful.

For large notebooks this causes user experience degradation (like tab switch being slow) as browser is busy rendering all the cells.

<!--
Thanks for contributing to JupyterLab!
Please fill out the following items to submit a pull request.
See the contributing guidelines for more information:
https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## References

<!-- Note issue numbers this pull request addresses (should be at least one, see contributing guidelines above). -->
https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/issues/9757
<!-- Note any other pull requests that address this issue and how this pull request is different. -->

## Code changes

<!-- Describe the code changes and how they address the issue. -->
To fix this I have tried rendering place holder cell's widget during [full idle frames](https://w3c.github.io/requestidlecallback/#idle-periods) (deadline.timeRemaining() will be 50) i.e., when there are no UI updates/user inputs queued. Increased timeout to avoid lot of cells getting idle callback at closer intervals and in case of timeout (meaning it couldn't find real idle time) instead of trying to render placeholder cell's widget, rescheduling to find another idle period.

These changes fixes sluggish UI for large notebooks.

Below is the benchmark report for [generated-1000cells-0.9ratio-2loc.ipynb](https://github.com/jupyterlab/benchmarks/blob/master/examples/from-script/generated-1000cells-0.9ratio-2loc.ipynb) notebook with 1K cells.

body:
## Motivation

To add DefaultFormatBundle to preprocess for SDK.

## Changed
**modified**
- csrc/preprocess/cpu/CMakeLists.txt
- csrc/preprocess/cuda/CMakeLists.txt
- mmdeploy/utils/export_info.py: remove the replacement from *DefaultFormatBundle* to *Image2Tensor*
**Added**
- csrc/preprocess/cuda/default_format_bundle_impl.cpp
- csrc/preprocess/cpu/default_format_bundle_impl.cpp
- csrc/preprocess/transform/default_format_bundle.cpp
- csrc/preprocess/transform/default_format_bundle.h
- tests/test_csrc/preprocess/test_default_format_bundle.cpp

## Note
I am not sure but I just dismissed `DC` part and label stuff for the **DefaultFormatBundle** in mmdet preprocess. Codes are below:
```python
    def __call__(self, results):
        """Call function to transform and format common fields in results.

        Args:
            results (dict): Result dict contains the data to convert.

        Returns:
            dict: The result dict contains the data that is formatted with \
                default bundle.
        """

        if 'img' in results:
            img = results['img']
            if self.img_to_float is True and img.dtype == np.uint8:
                # Normally, image is of uint8 type without normalization.
                # At this time, it needs to be forced to be converted to
                # flot32, otherwise the model training and inference
                # will be wrong. Only used for YOLOX currently .
                img = img.astype(np.float32)
            # add default meta keys
            results = self._add_default_meta_keys(results)
            if len(img.shape) < 3:
                img = np.expand_dims(img, -1)
            img = np.ascontiguousarray(img.transpose(2, 0, 1))
            results['img'] = DC(to_tensor(img), stack=True)
        for key in ['proposals', 'gt_bboxes', 'gt_bboxes_ignore', 'gt_labels']:
            if key not in results:
                continue
            results[key] = DC(to_tensor(results[key]))
        if 'gt_masks' in results:
            results['gt_masks'] = DC(results['gt_masks'], cpu_only=True)
        if 'gt_semantic_seg' in results:
            results['gt_semantic_seg'] = DC(
                to_tensor(results['gt_semantic_seg'][None, ...]), stack=True)
        return results

    def _add_default_meta_keys(self, results):
        """Add default meta keys.

        We set default meta keys including `pad_shape`, `scale_factor` and
        `img_norm_cfg` to avoid the case where no `Resize`, `Normalize` and
        `Pad` are implemented during the whole pipeline.

        Args:
            results (dict): Result dict contains the data to convert.

        Returns:
            results (dict): Updated result dict contains the data to convert.
        """
        img = results['img']
        results.setdefault('pad_shape', img.shape)
        results.setdefault('scale_factor', 1.0)
        num_channels = 1 if len(img.shape) < 3 else img.shape[2]
        results.setdefault(
            'img_norm_cfg',
            dict(
                mean=np.zeros(num_channels, dtype=np.float32),
                std=np.ones(num_channels, dtype=np.float32),
                to_rgb=False))
        return results
```

Fixes #3817 

## Problem Summary(Required) ：
<!-- (Please describe the changes you have made. In which scenarios will this bug be triggered and what measures have you taken to fix the bug?) -->

We will get a bad plan at startup for FE
The slow query explain：
```
PLAN FRAGMENT 0
 OUTPUT EXPRS:18: count | 1: lo_orderkey
  PARTITION: UNPARTITIONED

  RESULT SINK

  3:EXCHANGE
     limit: 1

PLAN FRAGMENT 1
 OUTPUT EXPRS:
  PARTITION: RANDOM

  STREAM DATA SINK
    EXCHANGE ID: 03
    UNPARTITIONED

  2:AGGREGATE (update finalize)
  |  output: count(4: lo_partkey)
  |  group by: 1: lo_orderkey
  |  limit: 1
  |  
  1:AGGREGATE (update serialize)
  |  group by: 1: lo_orderkey, 4: lo_partkey
  |  
  0:OlapScanNode
     TABLE: lineorder
     PREAGGREGATION: ON
     partitions=7/7
     rollup: lineorder
     tabletRatio=336/336
     tabletList=10037,10039,10041,10043,10045,10047,10049,10051,10053,10055 ...
     cardinality=1
     avgRowSize=8.0
     numNodes=0
```
When Fe startup, before the row count get from BE, the cost will makes no sense, we useually give a plan that does not seriously degrade performance. 

The optimizer choose 3 stage instead of 1 stage aggregate because of one stage will compute extra cost for multi_distinct_count function, but it's useless when table row count are not get from BE

author: danielwei15
body:
### Summary <!-- Required -->

This PR has two main changes.
- The first is to implement fetching club data from the backend (via a local fetch to localhost) and then to load that data into the clubs in ClubBoard.
- The second is to implement a responsive search bar that can match user-entered strings to club names (as of now, exactly, without any fuzziness or searching anything else).

To accomplish this, I restructured the App a bit. Since the NavBar sometimes contains a search bar and sometimes doesn't, I created an interface for props for the component, with one optional (a callback function for when the user changes the searched string) and one required (a boolean for whether the NavBar should render a search bar at all). This NavBar should now be placed as a child component of other pages, such as the ClubBoard or Registration page, which can pass in the appropriate prop(s) according to the need of the page.

### Test Plan <!-- Required -->

As a mostly frontend-centric PR, there's not too much testing to be done, but an issue I ran into that I tested via simple console logs was when the data from backend for rendering club tiles should be fetched. Doing it too often slows the app and makes us go over the Firebase limit for the day, but too rarely and the information could become outdated. I currently have it set to pull on ClubBoard's component mount.

### Notes <!-- Optional -->

The main takeaway from the slight restructuring is that the NavBar should now be a child component of other pages. This is already implemented, in this PR, for the existing components: ClubBoard and ClubRegistration.

### Breaking Changes  <!-- Optional -->

None (I believe).

author: imballinst
body:
This PR implements collapsible code block for other languages. Due to the nature of the metastring for normal code block, the plugin now "trims" the properties that are related to code title. This is done so that Prism.js will not duplicate the code title. The steps are as the following:

1. Parse the metastring
2. Wrap the code element using our `wrapWithMetastringElements` function
3. Trim the strings and keys that are related to the code title

author: liangxin1300
body:
When using systemctl to check service status over ssh, such return codes  are normal:
```
0 | program is running or service is OK
1 | program is dead and /var/run pid file exists
2 | program is dead and /var/lock lock file exists
3 | program is not running
4 | program or service status is unknown
```
So non zero return code with some no harm stderr output from ssh(such as with ssh banner configured), will trigger the condition to raise exception

author: herrnan
body:
In go-pas-client we convert the public models from the user to the interal models used for the actual request. In this conversion, when converting the band alarms list we do this:
```
for i, bandAlarm := range t.BandAlarms {
   threshold.BandAlarms[i] = bandAlarm.ToInternal()
}
```
This causes a problem when the ToInternal function on bandAlarm operates on a pointer to the struct rather than the struct itself. The function return an object with values that point back into the iterator variable and when we have more than one item in the list these values are set to the last value that was set in the iterator variable.

body: # Description This is a PR for developer portal page feature which is intended to fix this issue [#6](https://github.com/asumsi/inlive-website/issues/6). Our developer portal page layout consists of two main layout which is list.html and single.html inside `layouts/docs`: - list.html is a documentation layout for grouping specific content together. If we have several `guides` content, we can group it together inside `guides` folder and using `_index.md` file to declare the guides page to use the list page layout. Inside the `guides` folder we can create single content page for each guide. This list.html doesn't need an actual body content inside markdown because it will only render a list of pages inside the specific directory (section). - single.html is a documentation layout for a single documentation content, or we can call it a detail post page. Our convention when creating a single.html is by creating a directory for the content itself and put the `index.md` inside that content directory. My approach and implementation to create a structure for content can be seen in [this comment](https://github.com/asumsi/inlive-website/issues/6#issuecomment-1056125313). This is an example of how we can structure our content. Each individual documentation content both list page and single page content follows the front matter configuration that is defined inside [themes/inlive/archetypes/docs.md](https://github.com/asumsi/inlive-website/blob/851a5bf5be9e018c20ac3c7f88443a9cf8e2e2b6/themes/inlive/archetypes/docs.md?plain=1). We will use those configuration every time we create a new documentation content. For more explanation about the [archetypes/docs.md](https://github.com/asumsi/inlive-website/blob/851a5bf5be9e018c20ac3c7f88443a9cf8e2e2b6/themes/inlive/archetypes/docs.md?plain=1) configuration please see the README.md on [themes/inlive/archetypes/README.md](https://github.com/asumsi/inlive-website/blob/851a5bf5be9e018c20ac3c7f88443a9cf8e2e2b6/themes/inlive/archetypes/README.md) Besides the content, our developer portal page provides some features that help user navigate through the page: - Sidebar navigation menu The sidebar navigation menu has a collection of navigation links for each documentation content. This is useful because the user can see every documentation content that are available in the developer portal. We use [Hugo menu](https://gohugo.io/content-management/menus/) for defining the menu and menu items. Every menu item is defined in the front matter content separately. This is to ensure that the menu is connected with the page itself and if the page is deleted, the menu will also be deleted. For more detail about the implementation you can see [in this comment](https://github.com/asumsi/inlive-website/issues/6#issuecomment-1056148012). - Breadcrumbs The breadcrumbs is useful to give the navigation and information about the location of the page. - Next and Previous page link This is a feature to navigate the user between the documentation content. In order to create this feature we need to sort the order of every documentation page. We do the sorting by weight defined in the front matter. For more information please see [this comment](https://github.com/asumsi/inlive-website/issues/6#issuecomment-1056195292). README.md in the root project is updated. We added more information about creating a new content in Hugo. We also added step by step of creating a new documentation content. You can see it [here](https://github.com/asumsi/inlive-website/blob/851a5bf5be9e018c20ac3c7f88443a9cf8e2e2b6/README.md). Because our main content is pulled from Markdown file. We cannot control which element will be rendered from Markdown. If we do manual styling using CSS it will take a lot of effort. In order to overcome this issue we use official plugin from Tailwind called [@tailwindcss/typography](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/typography-plugin) to style the dynamic elements inside the Markdown without touching it directly. The design from Figma also follows this plugin design so we don't need to worry about the design. I wrote a comment related to this. You can see it [here](https://github.com/asumsi/inlive-website/issues/6#issuecomment-1058874050). **Additional Things:** - The `docs.js` file inside `themes/inlive/assets/js` is a Javascript assets that is only used on developer portal page. - We removed some dummy contents inside `docs` folder that are not needed anymore. - We moved `app-with-webrtc` content inside `content/docs/guides/app-with-webrtc/index.md` - To adjust with the current layout, I updated the [introduction](https://github.com/asumsi/inlive-website/pull/7/files#diff-d7be35564d277258fa6274c9f6f652c3815b8aa7e333ce0822fec1b09edcee8d) and [getting started](https://github.com/asumsi/inlive-website/pull/7/files#diff-02e757036064224c3fa4ad2e628ebd82e6475f8a24079b085425b4b304551bcd) content. Please kindly check. - We haven't implemented the table of content and search functionality yet. We will add these in the future. This PR removes the Metalsmith plugin [`metalsmith-headings-identifier`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/metalsmith-headings-identifier/v/0.0.2) and instead uses Marked to modify heading HTML. This removes a dependency from the `package.json` which has not been updated in 7 years. And while `metalsmith-headings-identifier` is quite opaque, the code is now much more obvious.

I've also tweaked the Marked code to generate hyperlinks. It used to be that any link other than to `developer.playcanvas.com` would open in a new tab. Now it's only links to anything other than `playcanvas.com`.

author: pprabhu-ng
body:
1. Avoid creating shadow filter when shadow opacity is not available.
      - Framework has non-zero default values for shadow offset.We draw shadow only when shadow opacity is non-zero.
      - So create shadowFilter only when shadow opacity is non-zero.
      - This will avoid bounds calculation when shadow is defined in app.
2. Focusable element can scroll usage 
      - Scrolling to next focusable element in  non-visible region . Currently,We check if the next focusable element is "contained" in next scrolling region.
      - We have to consider even if the focusable element is partially in next scrolling region.
3. Timing module 
      - When timer duration is very less and when we get create timer call in native , if this duration is already met . The target duration becomes negative value. For some reason, looks like folly does not handle negative value. 
      - So native timer module need to handle this and ensure we do not pass negative value to folly.

author: danielweck
body: https://turborepo.org/docs/getting-started # Without Turbo (PNPM recursive): `time pnpm build_` => `92.68s user 5.85s system 503% cpu 19.581 total` # With Turbo: 1) `time pnpm build` => `138.76s user 9.68s system 520% cpu 28.510 total` (cold run, no cache) 2) `time pnpm build` => `0.69s user 0.61s system 177% cpu 0.737 total` (subsequent run with full cache hit and "replay" of dist output + console log) I added the `clean-turbo` script in `package.json` to delete Turbo caches (alternatively, `--force` or `--no-cache` can be passed to `pnpm build` on the command line). Note that the original `build` script was excluding specific packages, but Turbo builds everything faster. PS: I fixed a Preact typings issue (JSX), and I updated the PNPM lockfile in order to work around a React typings conflict (multiple different versions in `node_module`). UPDATE: I added a Turbo-driven alternative to the `dev` script in the root `package.json`. The developer experience is improved thanks to Turbo caching, compared with Rollup's own watcher mode.

* autoDownload
* autoUpdate
* debug

author: ahmedetefy
body:
This PR:
- Adds parentheses to alias regex which is quite helpful to add as in the case of running conditional aggregate in queries over metrics, it is often required to disambiguate the columns returned depending on the aggregation, and the metric name 
- Adds backticks surrounding the alias

As an example, lets say we have a query like 
```
SELECT 
    sumMergeIf((value AS _snuba_value), equals((metric_id AS _snuba_metric_id), 150) AS sum,
    sumMergeIf((value AS _snuba_value), equals((metric_id AS _snuba_metric_id), 149)) As sum
FROM metrics_counters_local
WHERE ....
```
The most convenient way is to disambiguate these two fields in the query results is according to the aggregate and the metric name
If 150 -> session, and 149 -> user, then re-write this query as 
```
SELECT 
    sumMergeIf((value AS _snuba_value), equals((metric_id AS _snuba_metric_id), 150) AS sum(session),
    sumMergeIf((value AS _snuba_value), equals((metric_id AS _snuba_metric_id), 149)) As sum(user)
FROM metrics_counters_local
WHERE ....
```
I have spoken to @evanh about this, and he told me that if Clickhouse supports this (which it does), no reason why we shouldn't support it in our alias regex

body:
With the addition of LZO compression support to Jefferson, we discovered that our integration test cases for LZO were wrong.
    
What happened is that due to the lack of support for LZO, jefferson simply copied the compressed content into the output file. We did not catch that mistake during the early development of JFFS2 handlers.

This pull request also embarks a commit to refresh the lockfile, so I'm sure we're running the tests with the right version of jefferson.

```

# sudo podman run -d -p 6379:6379 \
    -v /var/lib/redis:/var/lib/redis/data:Z \
    registry.redhat.io/rhel8/redis-5
```

This PR aligns the haproxy config in the documentation with the redis deployment steps as well as the testing resource haproxy config and ansible deployment file.

body: I find that Corfu's auto completion is very useful when editing code, but not so much when editing prose.  It seems that currently auto completion is an 'all or nothing' type deal, but I'd really like it if it could be only be enabled for specific buffers.  With the changes in this PR, it's possible to write a trivial `prog-mode-hook` function that enables auto completion, but leaves it disabled for other kinds of buffers.  It seems to work well, but I suppose if this PR or some other code like it was to be merged, it would also necessitate some changes to the documentation.  Would a change like this be considered for merging into Corfu, or is this customisation not likely to be found beneficial enough to others to warrant this change in behaviour?

body:
# Newsletter section fixes

## Intent

- Replace placeholder image for _ConferenceUpdatesForm.tsx_ `'newsletter'`-type section 
- Deletes unused PlaceholderImage component
- Creates [/confirmation](https://structured-content-2022-web-pp63ilshf.sanity.build/confirmation) page in Studio

## Description

The [/confirmation](https://structured-content-2022-web-pp63ilshf.sanity.build/confirmation) page is added to match up with the current redirect that occurs when a user submits a previously non-subscribed email address into the `'newsletter'`-type form. Otherwise, this redirect would lead to a 404 after we merge `staging` to `master`. 

I looked throughout Mailchimp, but could not find the place where this redirect is configured. No matter; I like this solution because it means I don't have to prod any Sanity people to find and update this redirect. That also means the redirect won't properly work prior to launch, but it can still be accessed by visiting the path.

## Testing this PR

1. Verify that the [frontpage](https://structured-content-2022-web-pp63ilshf.sanity.build/) (and other pages) render the "final" image for the "Get conference updates" form in large viewports
2. Submit a previously non-subscribed email in the "Get conference updates" form and verify that you're redirected to /confirmation 
3. Verify that this matches the slug of the [Page](https://stagingadmin.structuredcontent.live/desk/page;2ef28313-b975-407f-9953-19a98a45cf84) and [Route](https://stagingadmin.structuredcontent.live/desk/route;8ea62f43-6009-4cc2-931f-09841af721f8) I created in Studio

body:
## Cause
When 'selectRecommendedContentForUri' is filtering results against the blocklist, it relies on claim data which could be unresolved yet. It filters to empty results for this scenario, hence the flashing message.

## Change
Just return raw results when claims are not resolved yet, so that the GUI knows it needs to show the placeholders while resolving. After resolving, it'll go through the blocklist filtering again.

author: oyvind-stenhaug
body:
# Tickets quickfixes

## Intent

Changes a couple small things with the Tickets component:
- Fixes a warning that was caused by a copy/paste error on my part, resulting in an invalid letter-spacing declaration
- Removes some `text-transform` usage that was presumably done as a hack/workaround for ticket features previously being all lowercase in Sanity

## Description

I find it really hard to tell the difference between letter-spacing being present or absent here, not sure if it's just me or if it's invisible to the naked eye… Removing the warning was the main thing here.

As for the ticket features, this appears to have been fixed on the studio side in https://github.com/sanity-io/structured-content-2022/commit/a52c12d8a96a07c55497cb574ef473fd306d069c so I don't think we need any workaround anymore (if we did we should probably only transform `::first-letter`, or adjust the content itself instead of in the styling layer, so that e.g. copy/paste would work correctly in Firefox).

## Testing this PR
1. Open your web browser's dev tools and ensure that CSS warnings/errors are enabled in the console
2. Open the [front page](http://structured-content-2022-web-git-tickets-quickfixes.sanity.build/) and then [/registration-info](http://structured-content-2022-web-git-tickets-quickfixes.sanity.build/registration-info)
3. Verify that there is no message along the lines of `Error in parsing value for ‘letter-spacing’.  Declaration dropped.` (quoted wording is from Firefox, other browsers may vary) in the dev tools console
4. Scroll down to the event pricing table and verify that the row headers are capitalized correctly, e.g. saying "Recordings after the event" and not "Recordings After The Event"

author: akinomyoga
body:
### Problem to solve

I have initially faced with some strange behavior of Terminology in a complicated setup, but I finally narrowed down the problem. For example, when the cursor state is restored by `DECRC` or `DECRST(1049)` after a character is outputted at the end of the screen (i.e., the last column of the bottom line), a redundant newline is inserted in the restored position even when the restored position is not at the end of the line. A reduced reproducer is

```bash
bash$ printf 'O\e7\e[%d;%dHA\e8K\n' $LINES $COLUMNS
```

Although we expect the output `OK` (without newlines between `O` and `K`), Terminology inserts a newline between `O` and `K` as follows:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8982192/156759203-719bb7ba-863e-4f14-a3ad-ddc627ae8e46.png)

This is because the state `ty->termstate.wrapnext` is preserved even after the cursor position is restored. This also causes other problems. For example, the state `wrapnext` at the time of saving the cursor state is lost after restoring the cursor state.

### Fix

The state `wrapnext` should be considered to be a part of the cursor state. In this PR, I have moved the bitfield `wrapnext` from `struct _Term_State::wrapnext` to `struct _Term_Cursor::wrapnext` (see commit a3f9887e) and changed `term_cursor_save` to save/restore also the `wrapnext` state (commit a0a22382). The result with the fixed Terminology behaves as expected as follows:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8982192/156760097-b8d8120e-d172-4a2b-948b-6f3b5335625b.png)

<!-- By the way, the identifiers starting with underscore plus a capital letter are reserved for the C implementations by the C standard, so they should not be used in application programs in general. However, they are used for tag names of `struct` and for the include guards in the codebase of Terminology. -->

## Tests (2022-03-04 update)

Test hashes have been updated in commit 0f40fb48.

The validity of the test results of the new binary has been checked by 9dc01ee9 (which is just for the check using the old data so not included in this PR). If you would like to test it in your environment, you can use [the branch `fix-cursor-restore-glitch.check`](https://github.com/akinomyoga/terminology/tree/fix-cursor-restore-glitch.check) in [`akinomyoga/terminology`](https://github.com/akinomyoga/terminology).

- [x] Branch is up-to-date with the branch to be merged with, i.e. `dev`
- [x] Build is successful
- [x] Code is cleaned up and formatted

### Summary

If you try to `INSERT INTO ... VALUES` with too many items, the MySQL server "goes away" and crashes the next query. "Too many" is somewhere between 100k and 400k: 100k runs, 400k does not. There are ways to address this in client and server settings, but to be less invasive, this PR splits the `VALUES` into 100k chunks.

# Commenting on Pull Requests As a collaborator on a repository, you will get and give pull request reviews before merging code. This is important! It ensures quality code and maintains momentum of changes to your project. As you can see, I've opened this pull request and requested you as a reviewer. Pull requests are places to _share_ the changes made to the repository. ### Responsibilities of a reviewer As a pull request reviewer, your role is to help the pull request author (thats me!) by making sure: - Code destined for production is of the highest quality - Intentional shortcuts (technical debt) are commented on and confirmed - The greater team is aware of potential risks associated with changes These broad responsibilities can include more specific goals, like: - Pointing out potential issues in code quality, security, or business logic - Suggesting other reviewers to the author, when warranted - Commenting on, approving, or requesting changes on the PR - Providing suggestions for alternate or better implementation details Some repositories use a [CODEOWNERS](https://help.github.com/articles/about-codeowners/) file. The `CODEOWNERS` file assigns responsibility for certain parts of the code to specific individuals or teams. When the `CODEOWNERS` feature is enabled, only the code owner has the final authority to approve the pull request. Your review may not be a formal approval, but it does show confidence. ## Step 2: Communicate in pull requests When an approval or request for changes is not yet needed, consider using **comments**. Comments enable you to inquire about the proposed change early in the review process. You don't need to wait until something is complete to make suggestions. ### :keyboard: Activity: Comment on my pull request 1. On the pull request, click **Files changed** 1. author: stephentoub
body:
During and post-parsing, we apply various optimizations to the regex node tree, in particular trying to annotate as much as possible as atomic in order to eliminate unnecessary backtracking.  Then later when RegexCompiler and the source generator view the final tree, they also compute for every node whether a child may backtrack, as doing so enables avoiding unnecessary backtracking-related code generation if the child is known to not backtrack (e.g. because it's now marked as atomic).  However, things can go awry if the compiler / source generator's view of what's atomic differs from what's actually generated.  Because of how optimizations are applied to the node tree, it's possible for a late optimization to make a transformation that then would enable a node to be made atomic, but we don't run that phase of the optimizer again, and thus the node is left non-atomic.  Then the source generator comes along, does its analysis, and sees that the node should be treated as atomic.  That leads to problems, because the node itself will have unnecessary backtracking code generated but the parent will rightly assume there wasn't anyway and won't generate the code necessary to compensate for it, or alternatively will generate code that causes problems (e.g. the source generator uses this information to determine whether it can output scopes).

Our outer loop tests that source gen our full regex corpus caught a case where this was happening.  A couple fixes, either of which on their own is sufficient to address this particular case, but each of which also brings other benefits:
1. When rendering a single-char loop, it consults the computed atomicity table to determine whether the rest of the source generation views it as atomic.  If it does, it instead does an atomic rendering.
2. When we do our ending backtracking elimination pass (i.e. walking down the right-hand side of atomic nodes to make anything that ends them also be atomic), we should also recur into lookarounds.

This also removes some duplicated code for reducing lookarounds, and renames some stale method names.

author: maroneze
body:
This PR adds 'since' information to compiler warnings, so that it can be printed in the user manual.

I'm not sure if all warnings should have a `since` tag; the numbered compiler options were introduced in 3.12, so I considered those as "pre-existing" warnings, and added tags only for warnings introduced in OCaml 4.00 and later. Hence why I used a `string option` instead of a `string`. It could be extended to older versions, if preferred.

The version information was obtained by checking out the Git tags corresponding to releases (4.00.0, 4.01.0, etc) and looking at the `t` definition in the `warnings.ml` file. I did not check for "patchlevel" releases (4.00.1, for instance), since I believe they never introduced new warnings.

For display purposes, I used the format `[since <version>]`, between brackets. That could cause issues with some regexes, if people were expecting the only brackets in the line to be those containing the name of the warning.

deployment preference hooks MUST have a function name that begins with
'CodeDeployHook_', hence the name for the PreTrafficHook lambda. If this
prefix isn't present, then the lambda is not granted the permissions to
write its validation status back to CodeDeploy.

Also includes a fix for the lambda, where an extra JSON parse needed to
be performed.

This is our most optimal (but not necessarily optimum) implementation of SGEMM.

There are two versions: 

SGEMM Data Parallel, where each tile computes a 16x16 block

SGEMM Group Cooperative, where each tile works with its NxN neighbors to compute an 16Nx16N block

The latter is more optimized.

Merging this in now to avoid letting it get stale.

author: maowtm
body:
This basically treats `from("scratch")` as any other image in order to simplify buildkit-frontend logic. buildkit.rs will "resolve" those by building the following Dockerfile:
```Dockerfile
FROM scratch
```
and the frontend would use `Source::image(id)`, where `id` is the empty image just built.

The alternative is to use [`buildkit_llb::ops::exec::Mount::Scratch`](https://docs.rs/buildkit-llb/latest/buildkit_llb/ops/exec/enum.Mount.html#variant.Scratch) whenever the parent is `from("scratch")`, but with this approach, due to the limit of the buildkit_llb rust library, it is not possible to output `from("scratch")` as the final image.

Note that, also due to poor library design, [`resolve_image_config`](https://docs.rs/buildkit-frontend/latest/buildkit_frontend/struct.Bridge.html#method.resolve_image_config) will fail when the image is empty. This is worked-around by treating FromScratch specially.

author: matt-bernhardt
body:
This does three things - and I debated whether to split this PR up, but have decided for now to keep them together:

1. Updates tooling for Composer to be able to install this plugin successfully.
2. Updates the plugin logic to make the plugin less dependent upon Advanced Custom Fields, and an "urgent" flag being defined.
3. General improvements (since I'm touching a bunch of files anyway)

## Updated tooling
This change involves:
- The YML workflows in `.github/workflows` for code validation (to replace Travis) and the build step.
- Updates to `composer.json` and `composer.lock`
- Removing `.travis.yml` and the badge from the readme
- Adding the vendor path to `.gitignore`
- Updates to the `codesniffer.*.xml` files

## Less dependency upon Advanced Custom Fields
- The querying logic within the class has been split, depending on whether a new `context()` method returns true or false. This context check determines whether ACF is enabled, and whether our specific urgent flag has been defined or not.
- If the context is "true" and these things are present, the existing logic is run. This means two queries, one for pending posts _with_ the urgent flag set, and then another for pending posts _without_ that flag set.
- If the context is "false" and those things are _not_ present, then only one query is performed, for all pending posts.
- This change means a bit more complexity in the `widget.php` template in case the "urgent" query was not run.
- The name of the widget also changes now if the context is "false", to remove a reference to a non-existent urgent status.

The widget with context "true"
![Screen Shot 2022-04-01 at 4 27 08 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1403248/161336619-1d8d34e1-493e-49ac-8436-26c069cc60a7.png)

The widget with context "false"
![Screen Shot 2022-04-01 at 4 27 41 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1403248/161336691-51292226-623c-40a7-8da2-157f158d293d.png)

## General improvements
- Turning off the CamelCaseMethodName check within CodeClimate.
- Whitelisting a few methods from specific checks that CodeClimate was flagging
- Code indenting changes within `widget.php`

## To see the updates in action:
See Matt for logins to these applications:
- [Prototype application without ACF present](https://pr-11-mitlib-prototype.pantheonsite.io)
- [Prototype with ACF and the Urgent flag installed](https://pr-24-mitlib-prototype.pantheonsite.io)

## Requires new or updated plugins, themes, or libraries?
YES for local development

## Requires change to deploy process?
NO - the existing deploy will work fine, but it also now can be deployed by Composer.

author: michaelbell
body:
The `clocks_init` function in the SDK unconditionally sets up the external crystal and PLLs.  This function is called as part of runtime_init before the user's main function.

It would be nice to be able to override this behaviour so that the system could be started from ROSC only, or simply to avoid bringing up the PLLs.  This would make it straightforward to create a project that did not use an external crystal using the standard SDK.

I propose to fix this by making the `clocks_init` function weak.  The user project can then provide their own version that configures ROSC and the clocks they need appropriately, and their version will be preferred by the linker.

This PR adds support for environment-specific configurations, for which I had 2 goals...

- different settings for the dev and prod environments (not just "production" vs "development" builds, which refer to the type of build rather than an environment)
- cascading settings so that we don't have to duplicate settings in a bunch of different configs and we're only overriding the default settings in a specific environment

This solution seemed clean and intuitive and easily integrated into the existing app.

author: jmcshane
body:
In theory, a session store could return multiple `Set-Cookie` headers from the request backend, so the tester library should support migrating all these cookies from the response to the request.

This PR updates the code to grab all cookies from the response and pass them to the subsequent request.

author: noelstephensunity
body: This is a very minor addition to the NetcodeIntegrationTest class that allows one to enabled verbose debugging.  The internal verbose debugging will log when TestRunner has entered into specific stages of the integration test itself.  The VerboseDebug method can also be used within a child derived class to log verbose information about the integration test for troubleshooting purposes without having to add child-class specific verbose logging code.  To enable verbose debugging, override OnSetVerboseDebug and return true.

author: malishav
body:
This PR introduces a public function p256_calculate_w that is useful in the context of compact EC point representation. The function calculates coordinate `w` that corresponds to `+y` or `-y` coordinate of a P256 point. For more details, see RFC6090, Appendix C. 

The PR, at this point in time, passes two test vectors:

* calculates `gy` (`w`) corresponding to `gx` in RFC 6090, Appendix D
* calculates `y` coordinate corresponding to the `x` coordinate of a valid point found in the existing `point_validation` test suite

The PR is noted as WIP because I still did not make my application work, and some additional changes may be required.

author: bg451
body:
Hey y'all! 

First off I want to say thank you so much for putting this together, this has saved me god knows how many hours!

This PR adds support for using googleapi URLs for GCS objects instead of creating signed URLs. We have a use case for a provider that's published on a public bucket, so the additional perms for blob signing were not needed. One thing to call out is that this is a breaking change, as users that rely on blob signing will need to specify `--storage-gcs-signedurl=true` to maintain the current behavior. However, to maintain compatibility the default for providers could be set to true unless explicitly specified to be false.

author: mdsmarte
body:
The tracking utils were refactored in PR #1576. Part of this refactor aligned the `n_frames` and `frame_count` attribute names, which represent the same concept, across the `SORT*` classes. The `SORTBase` class declares this attribute as `n_frames` but the `SORTSkeleton.track()` method still accesses it as `frame_count`. This causes an attribute error to be raised when using the skeleton tracking method: `AttributeError: 'SORTSkeleton' object has no attribute 'frame_count'`

This PR is a short fix to use the correct attribute name in the `SORTSkeleton.track()` method.

author: svonworl
body:
A CLI integration test had become very flaky and was essentially blocking development.  The problem was that all output sometimes did not completely propagate to the associated JUnit `SystemOutRule` and `SystemErrRule` objects, which the tests use to log `stdout`/`stderr`, so the test would sometimes retrieve an incomplete output and fail.  The theory is the logging system wasn't flushing, or the output was stuck in a queue/buffer and not processed by a logging thread in time, or something like that.

This PR adds a pause-and-flush before retrieving the logged stderr/stdout, via new extending classes `FlushingSystemOutRule` and `FlushingSystemErrRule`, which are instantiated as a replacement.

This PR fixes all tests in `dockstore-cli`.  Within `dockstore-cli`, there did not appear to be a good place to put the new `Flushing` classes so they were shared by both the unit tests and integration tests, so they are currently duplicated.  The same logging mechanism is used by tests in other repos, and in the interest of reducing flakiness, we should eventually fix those, too.  When we do that, we so should move the `Flushing` classes to package `io.dockstore.common` in `dockstore/dockstore-common`, at which point they'll be accessible from everywhere (I think).

The 500ms (half second) pause seems to work fine.  If we want to tighten it, we can run some experiments, it's not immediately apparent how long a pause is good enough.

author: kjuu0
body:
This PR implements the rest of the caching policies, some new algorithms, and also starts to track some different statistics.

Now when `cached_algos.py` is run, it benchmarks cached versions of quicksort, DFS, bubblesort, and permutation generation. Iterations/input size can be customized in main. After running, new folders suffixed with `{algo}_res` are created, and 3 types of graphs are generated:

`{algo}{cache_size}.jpg` shows the cache miss distributions of all eviction policies on `algo` with cache size `k`, displayed as a box plot so the median/quantile values are shown.

`{algo}_score{cache_size}.jpg` is a heatmap. You can think of it as a 2D matrix, where the `score` at coordinates `(policy_1, policy_2)` (coordinates in (row, column) format) means that `policy_1` beat `policy_2` `score`% of the time. Generally, `(policy_1, policy_2) = 1 - (policy_2, policy_1)`, although this is not always true because sometimes they perform the same. The numbers should be close to 1 usually though.

Finally, `{algo}_avg.jpg` shows how the average cache misses by eviction policy changes depending on cache size.

author: tshortli
body:
This PR is a rebase of https://github.com/apple/swift/pull/38988/. Original description:

Currently, the compiler assumes that all code in a module will only run when the minimum deployment target is satisfied. However, in modules using library evolution, this is only true for code that stays entirely inside the module's resilience domain. Anything that goes into the module interface, such as ABI-visible declarations and inlinable code, could affect the code generated in a module with a lower minimum deployment target, and could end up interoperating with older versions of the library built when it had a lower minimum deployment target.

This would be fine if the minimum deployment target never changed, but it's common practice to raise minimum deployment targets to reflect the minimum OS requirement of the current implementation, even if older versions of the module supported older OSes. The minimum deployment target essentially acts as a floor during availability checking, so all of the detail about old OS versions gets squashed away and ignored, even when checking code that will be inlined into other modules that can execute on those OSes. The result is that we do not reason correctly about which APIs will be available in the bodies of functions using features like `@inlinable` or `@_alwaysEmitIntoClient`. Uses that should be diagnosed as errors are instead allowed, causing us to compile code that won't work correctly when back-deployed.

This PR begins to address this by allowing you to base availability checking on a second, lower OS version number, except in parts of the code that are not externally visible. The idea is that, unlike the minimum deployment target, you would set this OS version when you first published the module and never raise it. At this point, the default behavior has not changed, but it probably ought to somewhere down the line.

Resolves rdar://89825739

After cloning the repo for the first time and often in CI, there is a delay where the project graph must be calculated to run nx commands.

<!-- This is the behavior we should expect with the changes in this PR -->

The Nx Project Graph is generated and cached during the `postinstall` phase of installing dependencies.

author: anthony-murphy
body:
This change unifies the removedClientId and removedClientOverlap into a single array, removedClientIds.

This simplifies our handling in a number of places, as we no longer need to check and manage both. In fact, there were a couple bugs where both were not handled appropriately. 

In addition, I've improved how we handle IRemovalInfo such that it is now all or nothing, which removes the need for a number of unsafe non-null assertions, and make the code simpler by removing the need to repeated non-null checks.

this may fix #9138, but it hard to know as we don't have much telemetry around the issue.

body:
Closes: #6140 

# Why

This PR adds proper sync support to adding, updating, and removing shipping lines.

# How

- Adds a new type `ShippingInputTransformer` to take care of updating an order given the shipping input.

- Make sure that we set the shipping `methodID` to `nil` when trying to delete a shipping line.

- Update the `containsLocalItems` method to take into account shipping lines & fee lines

- Update the `isIDLocal` method to consider `.zero` a local ID.

# Demo

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/562080/156852414-20651e67-5d13-4967-bc40-67d0c3c634a9.mov

# Testing Steps

- Set `orderCreationRemoteSynchronizer` feature flag to `true`
- Go to the new order screen.
- Adds a shipping fee & see the totals updated.
- Updates the shipping fee & see the totals updated.
- Remove the shipping fee & see the fee being removed.

---

### Description of your changes This PR adds External Secret Support as an alpha feature to Crossplane with the following changes: - Adds External Secret Store support to Composition types. - Propagates feature flags to provider controllers. - Adds finalizer and secret cleanup to `Composite reconciler`, to unpublish connection secrets (previously garbage collected with ownerrefs) - Adds secret cleanup to `Claim reconciler`, to unpublish connection secrets (previously garbage collected with ownerrefs) - Adds an initializer to create the `default` `StoreConfig` which publishes secret to Kube API with in cluster config. - Adds documentation for rolling out ESS support to existing Crossplane providers. Fixes #2881 I have: - [x] Read and followed Crossplane's [contribution process]. - [x] Run `make reviewable` to ensure this PR is ready for review. ### How has this code been tested #### Install and Configure Vault
Click to see exact steps Install ```shell kubectl create ns vault-system helm repo add hashicorp https://helm.releases.hashicorp.com helm upgrade --install vault hashicorp/vault -n vault-system ``` Initialize, Unseal and Configure ```shell kubectl exec -it vault-0 -c vault -n vault-system # To run in Vault container vault operator init # Note down the Initial Root Token vault operator unseal # Enter 1st of the 5 Unseal Keys outputted in the previous step vault operator unseal # Enter 2nd of the 5 Unseal Keys outputted in the previous step vault operator unseal # Enter 3rd of the 5 Unseal Keys outputted in the previous step # Verify that vault is initialized and unsealed vault status # Key Value # --- ----- # ... # Initialized true # Sealed false # ... # Login with root token vault login # Enter the Root Token noted down above # Enable Secret Engines v1 and v2 at paths /kvv1 and /kvv2. vault secrets enable -path=kvv1 kv vault secrets enable -path=kvv2 kv-v2 ```
#### Install Crossplane ESS enabled The following will install a locally built Crossplane from [this PR](https://github.com/crossplane/crossplane/pull/2940). ```shell kubectl create ns ```shell kubectl crossplane install provider turkenh/provider-gcp:v0.21.0-rc.13.g273ebf2 ``` Verify that External Secret Store feature enabled: ```shell kubectl -n crossplane-system logs --from-literal=token=$VAULT_TOKEN ``` Create a Secret `StoreConfig` for both Core Crossplane and Provider GCP: ```shell kubectl apply -f body:
### Describe the problem that is addressed by this PR

On client creation add a pipeline policy that configures the request agent to pass the Certificate. Also, the client factory has an overload that takes a Certificate credential. This is all autogenerated by codegen controlled with a flag

Generating new RLC package for Service Fabric. As part of supporting Client Certificate Authentication, there are a few changes in @azure-rest/core-client and @autorest/typescript generator.

@azure-rest/core-client
  * Expand ClientCertificate interface to allow passphrase, certificate-authority and pfx certificates
  * Add a pipeline policy to include the certificate to initiate the connection

@autorest/typescript
  * Add new `add-client-certificate` flag which adds the ClientCertificatePolicy to the Rest Client pipeline 


### What are the possible designs available to address the problem? If there are more than one possible design, why was the one in this PR chosen?
There were a couple of alternate designs discussed on how to support Certificate Authentication:
* Not provide anything and let users add the policy manually
* Expose a helper that users call to inject the certificate to the client i.e. `addClientCertificate(client, cert)`

However, the current approach offers a friendlier UX experience.

### Are there test cases added in this PR? _(If not, why?)_
Work in progress

### Command used to generate this PR:**_(Applicable only to SDK release request PRs)_
`rushx generate:client`

- [ ] Added impacted package name to the issue description
- [ ] Does this PR needs any fixes in the SDK Generator?** _(If so, create an Issue in the [Autorest/typescript](https://github.com/Azure/autorest.typescript) repository and link it here)_
